mainTopic: Can a person's נדר reach beyond his ownership, and can a נדר forbid things that do not exist yet (חילופין and גידולין) on another person?
overview: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about someone who says a house is קונם. אבימי asks: if an owner forbids his own house to someone and then dies or sells it, does the איסור stay? רבא brings a proof from a משנה about a father and son. If a father forbids his son from benefiting from him 'in my life and in my death,' the son may not inherit him. So a person can forbid something he owns even for the time after it leaves his ownership. Next the גמרא quotes a משנה. Someone who forbids fruit on himself is also forbidden in its חילופין (what it is traded for) and its גידולין (what grows from it). רמי בר חמא asks whether the same is true when the fruit is forbidden on someone else. He suggests that a person's power over others may be too weak to reach things that do not exist yet. His question continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: אבימי asks about a house that is forbidden and then leaves the owner's hands
steps.stepSummary: אבימי asks: if an owner says 'this house is קונם for you to enter' and then dies or sells it, is the visitor still forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the משנה, 'One who says to his friend, etc.' אבימי asked: If someone said, 'This house is קונם for you to enter,' and then he died or sold it to someone else, what is the law? Can a person forbid something he owns even for the time after it leaves his ownership, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about a house that is קונם. אבימי asks a new question: what if the owner himself forbids his house to another person and then loses ownership of it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner has full power over his house while he owns it. The question is whether that power can reach into the future, after the house belongs to his heirs or a buyer. If it can, the איסור stays even after he dies or sells.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used to make a נדר, making something forbidden like a קרבן
He asked (a real question, not an attack)
What is the law?
Something in his possession (that he owns)
For when it leaves his possession

steps.confusionAlert: In the משנה, the person making the נדר was the visitor forbidding the house on himself. Here it is the reverse: the OWNER forbids his house on the visitor.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an owner's נדר on his property keeps working after the property leaves his ownership

steps.title: רבא brings a proof from a father who forbids his son
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה: if a father forbids his son from benefiting from him, the son still inherits. But if the father said 'in my life and in my death,' the son does not inherit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. If someone says to his son, 'It is קונם that you may not benefit from me,' and then he dies, the son inherits him. If he said, 'in my life and in my death,' and then dies, the son does not inherit him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a משנה to answer אבימי's question. A father forbids his son from benefiting from his property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the father dies, his property is no longer his. It passes to the son through ירושה. Even so, when the father said 'in my death,' the son may not inherit. So the father's נדר keeps working after the property leaves his ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof)
Benefits
He inherits him

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
One who says to his son,

phrases.notes: Without the word 'death,' the נדר only covered the father's lifetime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אבימי's question with a proof from a משנה
steps.raayaObject: A person can forbid his property even for after it leaves his ownership
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a father who forbids his son 'in my life and in my death'

steps.title: Conclusion that a person can forbid his property for later
steps.stepSummary: From the father-son משנה, the גמרא concludes that a person can forbid what he owns even for the time after it leaves his ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: a person can forbid something in his possession for when it leaves his possession. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws the lesson from the משנה, and the גמרא agrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first 'שמע מינה' states the lesson. The second 'שמע מינה' accepts it as settled. So in אבימי's case, the visitor stays forbidden from the house even after the owner dies or sells it.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (said twice, it means the point is accepted)
Forbids

steps.whatToRemember: A person can forbid something he owns even for the time after it leaves his ownership. This is learned from the father who said 'in my life and in my death.'

phrases.english: Learn from this:

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An owner's נדר on his property keeps working after the property leaves his ownership

steps.title: משנה: forbidden fruit also forbids what replaces it and what grows from it
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches: if someone forbids specific fruit on himself, he is also forbidden in what it is traded for and in what grows from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: If someone says, 'This fruit is קונם upon me,' or 'It is קונם upon my mouth,' or 'It is קונם for my mouth,' he is forbidden in its replacements and in what grows from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה from elsewhere. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חילופין and the גידולין did not exist when he made the נדר. Even so, the משנה says a person who forbids fruit on HIMSELF is forbidden in them too. This is the base rule that רמי בר חמא will ask about.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Fruit or produce

Their growths (what grows from them if planted)

phrases.english: We learned there:

steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who forbids fruit on himself is also forbidden in its חילופין and גידולין

steps.title: רמי בר חמא asks about fruit forbidden on someone else
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks: if someone forbids fruit on another person, is that person also forbidden in the replacements?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: If someone said, 'This fruit is קונם on so-and-so,' what is the law about its replacements?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא takes the משנה's rule and asks whether it also applies when the fruit is forbidden on a different person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only spoke about someone forbidding fruit on himself. The new case is fruit forbidden on someone else, and the question is about the חילופין. Next he will explain why this case might be different.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who asks the question
So-and-so (some other person)
Forbidden upon so-and-so

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the משנה's rule and asks about a new case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חילופין are forbidden when fruit is forbidden on another person instead of on oneself

steps.title: The reasoning for why another person might be different
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא suggests a reason the rule might apply to oneself but not to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say this? Regarding himself: since a person can forbid his friend's fruit on himself, he can also forbid something not yet in the world on himself. Regarding his friend: since a person cannot forbid his friend's fruit on his friend, he also cannot forbid something not yet in the world on his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא explains one side of his question. He suggests that the rule about replacements may depend on how much power a person has over a נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may make another man's fruit forbidden on himself, even though he does not own it. So his power over himself is broad enough to cover things that do not exist yet, like the חילופין. He has no power to forbid someone's own fruit on that person. So perhaps his power over others is too weak to reach the not-yet-existing חילופין, and they would be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we say? (opens one side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not רמי בר חמא's final answer. It is one possible side of his question, and the question has not been settled yet.
